import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Conjecture 9.51

by D. J. S. Robinson

Does there exist a finitely presented soluble group satisfying the maximum
condition on normal subgroups which has insoluble word problem?

A finitely presented group is given by finitely many generators
$x_1, \dots, x_n$ and finitely many relators $r_1, \dots, r_m$ in the free
group on $x_1, \dots, x_n$; it is modelled here as `PresentedGroup rels`
for a finite set `rels` of elements of `FreeGroup (Fin n)`.

The word problem of a finitely presented group $G = \langle X \mid R \rangle$
asks for an algorithm deciding whether a word in the generators and their
inverses represents the identity of $G$. Solvability of the word problem
does not depend on the chosen finite presentation, so it can be tested on
the presentation defining the group.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

namespace Kourovka.«9.51»

/--
Does there exist a finitely presented soluble group satisfying the maximum
condition on normal subgroups which has insoluble word problem?

Here a group $G = \langle x_1, \dots, x_n \mid R \rangle$ with $R$ finite is

* *soluble* if its derived series reaches the trivial subgroup (`IsSolvable`);
* satisfying the *maximum condition on normal subgroups* (max-$n$) if every
  ascending chain of normal subgroups of $G$ is eventually constant, i.e. the
  poset of normal subgroups of $G$ is well-founded for $>$ (`WellFoundedGT`);
* of *insoluble word problem* if there is no algorithm deciding, for a word
  $w \in (X \cup X^{-1})^*$ in the generators and their inverses (a
  `List (Fin n × Bool)`), whether the image of $w$ in $G$ is the identity.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 3 20]
theorem kourovka.«9.51» : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∃ (n : ℕ) (rels : Set (FreeGroup (Fin n))), rels.Finite ∧
      IsSolvable (PresentedGroup rels) ∧
      WellFoundedGT {N : Subgroup (PresentedGroup rels) // N.Normal} ∧
      ¬ ComputablePred fun w : List (Fin n × Bool) =>
        PresentedGroup.mk rels (FreeGroup.mk w) = 1 := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«9.51»
attempts.decomposition_objections: None. The single-slot decomposition matches the statement.
modeling_decisions: 'Finitely presented group' is modelled directly as `PresentedGroup rels` with `rels : Set (FreeGroup (Fin n))` and `rels.Finite`, rather than an abstract `G` with `G ≃* PresentedGroup rels`. This is equivalent because solubility and max-n are isomorphism invariants and word-problem solvability is independent of the finite presentation (the witness is required to have undecidable word problem in its defining presentation).

'Maximum condition on normal subgroups' (max-n) is encoded as `WellFoundedGT {N : Subgroup G // N.Normal}` with the induced order (`Subtype.instLT`); by `wellFoundedGT_iff_monotone_chain_condition` this is exactly 'every ascending chain of normal subgroups is eventually constant'.

'Insoluble word problem' is encoded as `¬ ComputablePred (fun w : List (Fin n × Bool) => PresentedGroup.mk rels (FreeGroup.mk w) = 1)`: words in the generators and their inverses are `List (Fin n × Bool)` (`(a, true)` = a, `(a, false)` = a⁻¹), encoded via Mathlib's `Primcodable` instance; `ComputablePred` requires only classical existence of a decision procedure, so no constructive `Decidable` instance is needed.
'Soluble' is Mathlib's `IsSolvable` (derived series reaches ⊥).

Degenerate presentations (e.g. n = 0) yield groups with decidable word problem, so they cannot make the existential trivially true; `answer(True)` asserts a positive answer and `answer(False)` a negative one.
AMS tags 3 (mathematical logic/computability) and 20 (group theory).

Existing primitives (PresentedGroup, Set.Finite, IsSolvable, WellFoundedGT on the subtype of normal subgroups, ComputablePred with the Primcodable encoding of List (Fin n × Bool), FreeGroup.mk) suffice; no bespoke definitions.

/-!

by D. J. S. Robinson

Does there exist a finitely presented solvable group satisfying the maximum
condition on normal subgroups which has undecidable word problem?

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)

namespace Kourovka.«9.51»

/--
Does there exist a finitely presented solvable group satisfying the maximum
condition on normal subgroups which has undecidable word problem?

Here a finite presentation has generators indexed by `Fin n` and a finite set
`rels` of relators. Its word problem asks whether a word represents the
identity, equivalently whether its image in the free group lies in the normal
closure of `rels`. The maximum condition is expressed by well-foundedness of
strict inclusion on the type of normal subgroups.
-/

theorem kourovka.«9.51» : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∃ (G : Type) (_ : Group G) (n : ℕ) (rels : Finset (FreeGroup (Fin n)))
      (_ : G ≃* PresentedGroup (rels : Set (FreeGroup (Fin n)))),
      IsSolvable G ∧
        WellFoundedGT {N : Subgroup G // N.Normal} ∧
        ¬ComputablePred fun w : List (Fin n × Bool) ↦
          FreeGroup.mk w ∈ Subgroup.normalClosure (rels : Set (FreeGroup (Fin n))) := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«9.51»
modeling_decisions: A finite presentation is encoded by generators `Fin n`, a `Finset` of relators in `FreeGroup (Fin n)`, and a multiplicative equivalence from the witness group to the corresponding `PresentedGroup`.

The insoluble word problem is encoded as non-computability of the predicate on raw words `List (Fin n × Bool)` that their free-group image belongs to the normal closure of the relators, equivalently that they represent the identity.
The maximum condition on normal subgroups is encoded by `WellFoundedGT` on the subtype `{N : Subgroup G // N.Normal}`, which is the ascending chain condition under subgroup inclusion.

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Conjecture 9.51

by D. J. S. Robinson

Does there exist a finitely presented soluble group satisfying the maximum
condition on normal subgroups which has insoluble word problem?

Here a group is *finitely presented* if it is isomorphic to a group
$\langle x_1, \dots, x_n \mid r_1, \dots, r_m \rangle$ with finitely many generators
and finitely many defining relations. A group satisfies the *maximum condition on
normal subgroups* (max-$n$) if every non-empty set of normal subgroups has a
maximal element, i.e. every ascending chain of normal subgroups stabilises. The
*word problem* for a finitely generated group asks for an algorithm deciding, for a
word in a finite generating set, whether it represents the identity; its solubility
does not depend on the chosen finite generating set (or finite presentation).

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

namespace Kourovka.«9.51»

variable (G : Type*) [Group G]

/-- A group $G$ is *finitely presented* if it is isomorphic to a group
$\langle x_1, \dots, x_n \mid r_1, \dots, r_m \rangle$ given by finitely many generators
and finitely many defining relations, i.e. to the quotient of the free group on `Fin n`
by the normal closure of a finite set of relators. -/
def IsFinitelyPresented : Prop :=
  ∃ (n : ℕ) (rels : Finset (FreeGroup (Fin n))),
    Nonempty (G ≃* PresentedGroup (rels : Set (FreeGroup (Fin n))))

/-- A group $G$ satisfies the *maximum condition on normal subgroups* (max-$n$) if every
non-empty set of normal subgroups of $G$ has a maximal element; equivalently, every
ascending chain of normal subgroups of $G$ stabilises. -/
def HasMaxNormalSubgroups : Prop :=
  WellFoundedGT {N : Subgroup G // N.Normal}

/-- A group $G$ has *soluble word problem* if, for every finite generating family
$f \colon \{0, \dots, n-1\} \to G$ of $G$, the set of words in the letters $f(i)^{\pm 1}$
that represent the identity of $G$ is decidable.

A word is encoded as a list of pairs `(i, b) : Fin n × Bool`, where `(i, true)` stands for
the letter $f(i)$ and `(i, false)` for $f(i)^{-1}$; the word `w` represents the element
`FreeGroup.lift f (FreeGroup.mk w)` of $G$. For a finitely generated group this notion does not
depend on the choice of the finite generating family. -/
def HasSolvableWordProblem : Prop :=
  ∀ (n : ℕ) (f : Fin n → G), Subgroup.closure (Set.range f) = ⊤ →
    ComputablePred fun w : List (Fin n × Bool) => FreeGroup.lift f (FreeGroup.mk w) = 1

/-- A finite group satisfies the maximum condition on normal subgroups. -/
@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem hasMaxNormalSubgroups_of_finite [Finite G] : HasMaxNormalSubgroups G := by
  unfold HasMaxNormalSubgroups
  infer_instance

/-- The trivial group has soluble word problem. -/
@[category test, AMS 3 20]
theorem hasSolvableWordProblem_of_subsingleton [Subsingleton G] : HasSolvableWordProblem G :=
  fun _ _ _ => ⟨fun _ => isTrue (Subsingleton.elim _ _), Computable.const true⟩

/--
Does there exist a finitely presented soluble group satisfying the maximum condition
on normal subgroups which has insoluble word problem?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 3 20]
theorem kourovka.«9.51» : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∃ (G : Type) (_ : Group G),
      IsFinitelyPresented G ∧ IsSolvable G ∧ HasMaxNormalSubgroups G ∧
      ¬ HasSolvableWordProblem G := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«9.51»
attempts.decomposition_objections: None. The single-slot decomposition (one yes/no existence question) is correct; 'con-\\linebreak dition' is a hyphenation artifact for 'condition'.
modeling_decisions: Word problem solvability is defined relative to finite generating families (∀ finite generating family, the identity-word predicate is computable). Its negation therefore asserts that some finite generating family has an undecidable word problem. By the standard invariance theorem, for finitely generated (in particular finitely presented) groups, decidability of the word problem is independent of the finite generating set/presentation, so this is equivalent to the ∃-version and to the presentation-based version.

Words are encoded as `List (Fin n × Bool)` (Mathlib's raw free-group words, `(i, true)` ↦ generator, `(i, false)` ↦ inverse; verified in a scratch check) rather than elements of `FreeGroup (Fin n)`, since `FreeGroup` has no `Primcodable` instance; this is the classical formulation of the word problem anyway.
Finite presentation uses generators indexed by `Fin n` and a `Finset` of relators; this is fully general up to isomorphism.

Max-n is `WellFoundedGT` on the subtype of normal subgroups with the induced order (every non-empty set of normal subgroups has a maximal element ⇔ ACC), rather than the equivalent 'every normal subgroup is the normal closure of a finite set'.
The existential quantifies over `G : Type` (universe 0) following the convention of the other Kourovka files (1_74, 1_40).

namespace Kourovka.«9.51»

variable (G : Type*) [Group G]

/-- A group $G$ is *finitely presented* if it is isomorphic to a group given by
finitely many generators $x_1, \dots, x_n$ and finitely many relators
$r_1, \dots, r_m$ in the free group on $x_1, \dots, x_n$. -/
def IsFinitelyPresented : Prop :=
  ∃ (n : ℕ) (rels : Finset (FreeGroup (Fin n))),
    Nonempty (G ≃* PresentedGroup (rels : Set (FreeGroup (Fin n))))

/-- A group $G$ satisfies the *maximum condition on normal subgroups* (max-$n$) if
every non-empty set of normal subgroups of $G$ has a maximal element, i.e. the
relation $>$ on the normal subgroups of $G$ is well-founded. Equivalently, every
ascending chain $N_1 \le N_2 \le \dots$ of normal subgroups of $G$ is eventually
constant. -/
def SatisfiesMaxN : Prop :=
  WellFoundedGT {N : Subgroup G // N.Normal}

/-- A group $G$ has *soluble word problem* if it has a finite generating family
$g_1, \dots, g_n$ such that the set of words $w$ in the letters
$g_1^{\pm 1}, \dots, g_n^{\pm 1}$ with $w = 1$ in $G$ is decidable. Words are
encoded as lists of pairs (generator, exponent sign), and a word is evaluated in
$G$ by mapping it through the free group on `Fin n`. Solubility of the word
problem does not depend on the chosen finite generating family. -/
def HasSolvableWordProblem : Prop :=
  ∃ (n : ℕ) (f : Fin n → G), Subgroup.closure (Set.range f) = ⊤ ∧
    ComputablePred fun w : List (Fin n × Bool) => FreeGroup.lift f (FreeGroup.mk w) = 1

/-- A group given by finitely many generators and finitely many relators is
finitely presented. -/
@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem isFinitelyPresented_presentedGroup (n : ℕ) (rels : Finset (FreeGroup (Fin n))) :
    IsFinitelyPresented (PresentedGroup (rels : Set (FreeGroup (Fin n)))) :=
  ⟨n, rels, ⟨MulEquiv.refl _⟩⟩

/-- A finite group satisfies the maximum condition on normal subgroups. -/
@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem satisfiesMaxN_of_finite [Finite G] : SatisfiesMaxN G := by
  unfold SatisfiesMaxN
  infer_instance

/-- The trivial group has soluble word problem. -/
@[category test, AMS 3 20]
theorem hasSolvableWordProblem_unit : HasSolvableWordProblem Unit := by
  refine ⟨0, Fin.elim0, Subsingleton.elim _ _, inferInstance, ?_⟩
  exact (Computable.const true).of_eq fun w => by simp

Does there exist a finitely presented soluble group satisfying the maximum
condition on normal subgroups which has insoluble word problem?

That is, is there a group $G$ that is finitely presented, soluble, satisfies
max-$n$, and whose word problem is undecidable?
-/

      IsFinitelyPresented G ∧ IsSolvable G ∧ SatisfiesMaxN G ∧

theorem maxN_of_finite (G : Type*) [Group G] [Finite G] : MaxN G := by
  unfold MaxN
  infer_instance

/-- The word problem of the presentation $\langle x_0, \dots, x_{n-1} \mid \mathrm{rels} \rangle$:
a word $w$ in the letters $x_i^{\pm 1}$ (encoded as a list of pairs
$(i, \pm)$, where `(i, true)` is $x_i$ and `(i, false)` is $x_i^{-1}$) satisfies
`WordProblem rels w` if $w$ represents the identity of the presented group. -/
def WordProblem {n : ℕ} (rels : Set (FreeGroup (Fin n))) (w : List (Fin n × Bool)) : Prop :=
  PresentedGroup.mk rels (FreeGroup.mk w) = 1

/-- The word problem of the trivial presentation $\langle x_0 \mid x_0 \rangle$ is soluble. -/
@[category test, AMS 3 20]
theorem computablePred_wordProblem_singleton :
    ComputablePred (WordProblem {FreeGroup.of (0 : Fin 1)}) := by
  have h : ∀ w, WordProblem {FreeGroup.of (0 : Fin 1)} w := by
    intro w
    unfold WordProblem
    have : Subsingleton (PresentedGroup {FreeGroup.of (0 : Fin 1)}) := by
      refine ⟨fun a b => ?_⟩
      obtain ⟨a, rfl⟩ := PresentedGroup.mk_surjective _ a
      obtain ⟨b, rfl⟩ := PresentedGroup.mk_surjective _ b
      have key : ∀ x : FreeGroup (Fin 1), PresentedGroup.mk {FreeGroup.of (0 : Fin 1)} x = 1 := by
        intro x
        induction x using FreeGroup.induction_on with
        | C1 => simp
        | of i =>
          have : i = 0 := Subsingleton.elim _ _
          subst this
          exact PresentedGroup.one_of_mem rfl
        | inv_of i ih => simp [ih]
        | mul x y hx hy => simp [hx, hy]
      rw [key a, key b]
    exact Subsingleton.elim _ _
  exact ⟨fun w => isTrue (h w), (Computable.const true).of_eq fun w => by simp [h w]⟩

/--
Does there exist a finitely presented soluble group satisfying the maximum
condition on normal subgroups which has insoluble word problem?

A finitely presented group is `PresentedGroup rels` for finitely many generators
`Fin n` and a finite set of relators `rels`. Its word problem is insoluble if the
predicate "the word $w$ represents $1$" on words `w : List (Fin n × Bool)` is not

finite presentation, so the choice of presentation is immaterial.

by D. J. S. Robinson

normal subgroups all stabilize and whose word problem is undecidable?
